case_name: Smt. Meera vs Vijay Shankar Talchidia
facts_of_case: The parties were married in 1976, but no child was born. The husband sought divorce alleging cruelty and adultery. The wife denied the allegations.

legal_principles.principle: Cruelty as a ground of divorce under Section 13(1)(ia) is a conduct of such type that the petitioner could not reasonably be expected to live with the respondent.
legal_principles.held: Now, the act or omission or conduct which constitutes cruelty need not cause any sort of apprehension in the mind of the petitioner.

legal_principles.principle: Cruelty is a conduct of such type that the relations between the parties had deteriorated to such an extent due to the conduct of one of the spouses that it has become impossible for them to live together without mental agony, torture or distress.
legal_principles.held: It has not been defined in the Act as it was not possible to do so. Section 13(1)(ia) has undergone a change by 1976 amendment made by the Parliament.

legal_principles.principle: What may amount to cruelty in one case may not amount to cruelty in another case.
legal_principles.held: No rigid meaning can be assigned to cruelty in order to come under Section 13. What may amount to cruelty in one case may not amount to cruelty in another case.

legal_principles.principle: The court dealing with a petition for divorce under Section 13 is expected to bear in mind that the problem before it is that of human beings and that all psychological changes in a man's conduct has to be borne in mind before granting or rejecting the petition.
